Shopify Storefront Proposal

Roots Hair & Beauty — Shopify Storefront Proposal

Client: Roots Hair & Beauty — afro hair care, hair extensions, skincare, braids and make-up retailer (UK, GBP)
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup
Date: September 23, 2026
1

Proposed scope

1.1 Platform

Move the storefront to Shopify.

This proposal covers Shopify design & development only. Backend data migration (products, orders, customers) is not included — that's handled by a separate team, LitExtension (a sister brand), who provide their own estimate and quote once the volume to migrate is known.

1.2 Theme

Foundation theme for both options below: Ella — free through the Litos/HaloThemes partnership.

Ella is built for large-catalogue retail and ships beauty and cosmetics demo layouts, so a good share of the work below is theme configuration rather than custom development. Covered natively: grouped mega menu, compact sticky header, predictive search overlay, wishlist, Quick View, colour swatches on the product card, sidebar collection filtering, and multi-language / multi-currency support.

The store is built by customizing Ella, carrying over the existing brand identity — navy, pink and cream palette, and the Roots Hair logo.

1.3 Two options

  • Option 1 — Replicate & improve. The current site rebuilt on Shopify, with the UX and UI fixes in 1.5.
  • Option 2 — Redesign. Not bound by the current layout — a new design direction for the storefront, per 1.6.

Sections 1.4, 1.7, 1.8 and 1.9 apply to both options.

1.4 Core build

  • Theme setup & brand styling — Ella configured to the brand identity: navy, pink and cream palette, logo, typography.
  • Page templates — homepage, collection, product, cart, account and search, plus the content pages: Brands, Gallery, Contact, Terms & Conditions, Privacy Policy, Shipping Policy and Refund Policy.
  • Catalogue structure — the eight shopping categories (Hair Care, Hair Extensions, Party Wigs, SkinCare, Hair Accessories, Braids & Plaits, Make up & Fragrance, Kids) and their sub-categories set up as Shopify collections with navigation to match.
  • Collection filtering and sort — sidebar filters by category, brand, price and availability across a catalogue of 300+ products.
  • Free-shipping threshold — the £60 announcement bar carried over.
  • Responsive storefront — verified on desktop, tablet and mobile.
  • Full storefront review & testing before launch, so everything is verified working before the store goes live.

1.5 UX & UI improvements — Option 1

Beauty and hair care is a visually-led category, so the work concentrates on UX, UI and responsive behaviour.

Header & navigation

  • Logo into the header. The logo currently sits in its own band below the navigation; it moves into the header bar itself, alongside the menu, search, account, wishlist and cart.
  • Header height reduced. The header currently stacks four separate bands — announcement, menu row, search row, and a logo band — and on scroll the sticky header takes up roughly a third of the screen. It's rebuilt as a single bar that shrinks to a slim strip once the customer scrolls.
  • Menu rebuilt as a mega menu. The main row runs out of space and pushes the last items behind a › arrow while the whole right-hand half of the bar sits empty. Categories group into dropdown panels so every category is reachable in one action.
  • Language switcher moved into the header row.

Mobile header

Rebuilt for mobile: logo in the bar, hamburger, search, account, wishlist and cart, with the language selector inside the menu drawer — in place of the current stack of a pink bar, a separate language row and a separate logo row before any content appears.

Colour

The palette works and is on brand. A few elements sit off-tone against it — most visibly the lilac and lime call-to-action buttons on the product page. Primary and secondary CTAs are restyled to the brand navy and pink, applied consistently across product cards, product pages, cart and forms.

Newsletter block

The "Discover More" block is rebuilt — the field label currently overlaps the supporting line above it.

Footer

Rebuilt with flat link columns — no dropdown menus in the footer — plus contact details, social row, newsletter signup, payment icons and a legal bar.

On mobile the footer block doesn't run the full width of the screen; it's rebuilt to fill the viewport.

Collection & product pages

  • Product cards restyled to the brand palette, with hover image swap, Quick View and a wishlist icon.
  • Variant selection shown as swatches and buttons on the card and on the product page, instead of the current dropdowns.

Homepage imagery

Homepage banners are rebuilt on a consistent grid with a consistent crop and background treatment — several of the current banners use rough cut-outs that undercut the finish of the page.

1.6 Option 2 — Redesign

Not bound by the current site's layout or structure:

  1. Full UI/UX and information-architecture redesign for a 300+ product beauty catalogue.
  2. Homepage, navigation, collection page and product page rebuilt around product discovery and conversion rather than around the existing structure.
  3. Mobile-first, with the visual polish the beauty and hair care category expects — imagery, spacing, typography and motion treated as part of the design, not as an afterthought.
  4. Ella (1.2) as the foundation theme, customized to the new design direction.
  5. Brand identity — logo, palette and tone — preserved, in a modern visual direction.

1.7 Apps & integrations

  • Wishlist — covered by Ella natively. No app and no monthly fee.
  • Live chat — Shopify Inbox, free, set up and placed on the storefront.
  • Multi-language — Shopify Translate & Adapt, free. It auto-translates up to two languages and takes unlimited manual translations beyond that, and covers products, collections, pages, navigation and SEO fields. Setup is included; translation copy itself is not.

1.8 Optional — not included in the effort below

Hair care and skincare consumables are repeat purchases, so two additions are worth considering for retention:

  • Bundles / buy-as-a-set — routine or regimen sets sold as one purchase.
  • Loyalty points — points on purchase, redeemable against future orders.
Effort for these has not been estimated and isn't part of the totals in section 2. Either would be scoped and quoted separately once confirmed.

1.9 Notes

  • Imagery: product and campaign photography is supplied for implementation. This proposal covers building the storefront, not photography production or retouching.
  • Theme, Shopify subscription, payment gateway/shipping setup: standard scope notes — theme and Shopify plan are subscribed to/purchased directly by the client; payment gateway and shipping carrier setup handled by the client's own team for credential confidentiality (a setup guide can be provided).
